title: Digby man dies in police custody after altercation
article: RCMP said officers used batons, pepper spray and a Taser gun to try and detain a Nova Scotia man who died in their custody Friday.
Paul Sheldon Saulnier, 42, of Digby died outside of the Digby RCMP detachment at around 4 p.m. local time.
He had been placed under arrest for a previous offence and fled the detachment while being fingerprinted.
The Mounties said the man resisted the three officers who followed him outside into the parking lot.
"They tried verbally to tell him to come back in, and then they started to go through their levels of force," RCMP Const. Joe Taplin told ATV news on Saturday.
During the struggle, police also removed Mr. Saulnier's boots because he was kicking them, and then they handcuffed him.
Once Mr. Saulnier was handcuffed, an officer noticed his breathing was shallow, said Mr. Taplin.
Emergency officials were called and Mr. Saulnier was pronounced dead at the scene.
Alfred Saulnier, Paul Saulnier's father, accused police of mishandling the situation.
"The boy didn't need to die for no reason," he told ATV news.
He said if he isn't satisfied with the results of a police investigation, he would launch a private investigation of his own.
An independent investigation team, led by a senior member of the Halifax Regional Police and involving RCMP members from other areas of the province, was set up to examine the incident.
The officers involved were put on leave until the investigation was complete.
An autopsy was conducted on Saturday, but the results were not yet available.
